description: A list comprehension builds a list from each item of another, as Python writes it, and means exactly the map call with a lambda
code:
prices = [12, 30, 8]
doubled = [price * 2 for price in prices]
[doubled, prices.map(price => price * 2)]

description: An if clause keeps only the items whose condition holds, exactly a filter call before the map
code:
scores = [40, 75, 90, 55]
[score + 5 for score in scores if score >= 60]

description: A comprehension stays live on its source list and on the variables its expression and condition read
code:
prices = [12, 30, 8]
limit = 10
picked = [price * 2 for price in prices if price > limit]
prices.push(40)
limit = 5
picked

description: A comprehension over a class reads its population and follows new instances and changed properties
code:
class Order(item, qty):
    this.item = item
    this.qty = qty
bulk = [order.item for order in Order if order.qty >= 3]
Order("pen", 1)
ink = Order("ink", 4)
Order("cap", 5)
ink.qty = 2
bulk

description: The of keyword spells the same comprehension as in, the way JavaScript loops write it
code:
readings = [17, 21]
[[reading * 2 for reading of readings], [reading * 2 for reading in readings]]

description: Inside its brackets a comprehension may span lines, and comprehensions nest when each lambda reads only its own name
code:
grid = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
scaled = [
    [cell * 10 for cell in row]
    for row in grid
]
scaled

description: The element may be a Python-style conditional expression, while a conditional used as the source needs parentheses
code:
scores = [40, 90]
fallback = [0]
["high" if score > 80 else "low" for score in (scores if scores.length > 0 else fallback)]

description: A comprehension renders as the filter and map calls it means, so why explains it with that rule
code:
stock = [3, 0, 7]
listed = [qty * 2 for qty in stock if qty > 1]
(why listed).map(step -> step.rule)

description: Its lambdas cannot read the parameters of an enclosing function, so a comprehension in a function reads them only as its source
